hypotheses.statement: If one transcribed species behaves as a scaffold and another as a weaker-binding adsorbent, composition-dependent adsorption/wetting at interfaces inside a scaffold-rich RNA network could stabilize RNA-poor internal domains that appear as cavities. This extends the external/coexisting-phase interface relation reported for a different two-RNA/PEG system to internal domains in the present transcribing condensate. Neither case species roles nor internal cavity formation is established. At fixed reaction chemistry, measured RNA loading should change species-resolved interface enrichment and, if the bridge is correct, cavity incidence/area.

The measured phase endpoints are not comparable to the imaging reaction or its mixture range; cavities instead arise from amplification carryover or another reaction-state change independently of composition-driven domains. Constant selectivity under matched conditions remains possible.

gaps.description: Determine whether measured RNA composition changes partitioning or interface wetting under matched conditions and whether that predicts internal cavities. Neither the composition response nor the cavity mapping is identified.
No mapping from bulk phase concentrations/volumes or interfacial enrichment to image f, and no causal separation from carryover or population/measurement alternatives.

equations: A possible interface measurement is Gamma_i=integral_over_interface(c_i(local)-c_i(bulk reference)) dz; no concentration profile, interfacial thickness, or surface excess is supplied, so this is a measurement definition, not an evaluated law.
At dense-phase volume fraction phi, dense-phase variant mass fraction=phi*Cv_dense/[phi*Cv_dense+(1-phi)*Cv_dilute]; it is not f and requires phase volumes.

Conditional prediction: at fixed chemistry and controlled x_v_over_r, a scaffold/adsorbent pair predicts composition-dependent interface enrichment/wetting. Cavity incidence/area should covary with loading only if the proposed internal-domain bridge holds.

S1 wetting may be specific to its reported purine-rich/pyrimidine-rich RNA and PEG conditions; transfer to these four-arm RNA products is unestablished.
predictions: H1: in a fixed-chemistry, assay-matched RNA loading series, species-resolved interface enrichment/wetting should vary with measured x_v_over_r; cavity incidence/area should covary if internal wetting drives the cavities. Measure phase volumes and use fixed imaging rules.
H0: matching carryover/reaction state explains cavity differences without requiring interface enrichment or alpha to vary with RNA loading.

The existing phase endpoints conditionally differ in selectivity but cannot test either prediction because loading order, assay matching, phase volumes, local interface composition, and longitudinal cavity state are missing.

final.question_and_reason: Can composition-dependent RNA partitioning and interface wetting create persistent internal RNA-poor cavities in the transcribing condensate? This is the most concrete mechanism gap because the case has image trajectories, phase endpoints, and length-fraction endpoints, but no matched link among RNA composition, interfaces, and cavity state.
final.increment: Formulated an explicit wetting-mediated internal-domain hypothesis with a distinct carryover/constant-selectivity alternative. Interpreted measured partition arithmetic and two background searches without overclaiming abstracts.
final.new_hypotheses: H1: conditional on one case RNA acting as scaffold and another as weaker-binding adsorbent, composition-dependent wetting at internal interfaces stabilizes RNA-poor domains that appear as cavities. H0: carryover/reaction-state change explains cavities without composition-dependent wetting; phase endpoints may not transfer.
final.actual_derivation_or_computation: Executed C2L1-alpha: alpha=K_variant/K_ref, where each K is dense/dilute concentration. At tie-line 1 alpha=37.863 with rectangular marginal bounds [4.769,300.647]; at tie-line 2 alpha=0.335 with bounds [0.0422,2.661]; tie-line 0 variant K undefined. Units cancel, so alpha is dimensionless. The intervals are disjoint, but this comparison assumes assay comparability; tie-line index does not establish composition order and bounds are not confidence intervals. No second computation was run.
final.discriminating_prediction: In a fixed-chemistry, carryover-matched series spanning directly measured RNA loading, H1 predicts species-resolved interface enrichment/wetting will change with loading and cavity incidence/area will covary under fixed imaging rules; H0 predicts carryover/reaction-state matching explains the cavity phenotype without requiring that loading-interface-cavity relationship.
final.evidence_support_conflict_untested: Support: C2L1-alpha endpoint calculation; E02 single-preparation length-fraction endpoint differences; S1 abstract reports interfacial wetting in a different two-RNA/PEG system. Conflict/limits: tie-lines are not a controlled composition series; tie-line 2 bounds overlap unity; S1 reports no internal cavities; focused C2L3 query returned zero sources; C03 lacks longitudinal cavity state; DNA read fractions do not give RNA abundance; carryover is unmeasured.
final.decision: The arithmetic and literature-review tasks are complete. The main mechanism gap G1 is unresolved; retain H1 as a candidate hypothesis and do not claim causal confirmation or reject H0.
final.dissent: Interface wetting is a plausible module, but the extension from external/coexisting interfaces to internal cavities in this transcription system is unsupported. Zero search hits are not evidence of absence.
final.next_experiment: Use fixed reaction chemistry with carryover-matched controls and a measured RNA mixture-loading series. Quantify RNA species in both phases and at interfaces, phase volumes, and longitudinal per-droplet cavity area/state across independent preparations with fixed segmentation.
final.limitations: Only one broker computation was executed. Phase endpoint bounds are rectangular marginal bounds, not statistical intervals; no composition-time series, phase volumes, local cavity concentrations, causal controls, or longitudinal cavity tracks are available. Literature results are abstracts, and the focused query returned zero hits.
